passage:
The school film club held a silent movie night. Some students thought silent movies would be boring because there were no spoken words.
Before the movie began, the club leader explained that old silent movies used music, facial expressions, and body movements to tell stories.
At first, students laughed at the fast movements. Soon, they became quiet. They began to notice small details: raised eyebrows, quick footsteps, and hands reaching for a door.
After the movie, one student said, "I understood more than I expected."
The club leader smiled. "Words are useful," she said, "but they are not the only way to speak."
The night taught students to watch more carefully, not only listen.
